_comment: COUPLING tier-2. The description of the `couple` tool's DEFAULT accelerator — "'aitken' — theta adapts per participant, starting from the theta you pass, clamped into [0.05, 1.0]" — is three independent assertions in one sentence, and none had ever been run. UNIT LEVEL, and said plainly because it carries less weight than a coupling: the two BOUNDS are pinned by calling core.coupling_driver._aitken directly with residual vectors chosen so the unclamped rule theta = -theta_prev*<r_old,dr>/<dr,dr> lands around -50/+50 and -1000/+1000, far outside the interval in both directions, and the returned theta must be EXACTLY the bound, no tolerance, because it is a min/max against a literal; a third call whose unclamped value is 0.25 must come back unchanged, so a driver that clamped everything to one number could not satisfy all three. A two-participant conduction problem cannot be steered out of range on demand, which is why that part is a unit call. END TO END, everything else: a real coupling through the registered `couple` tool at rho=4, theta0=0.5, checked against the closed-form interface temperature and flux from both sides plus the conservation balance, and from it — that the number of adaptations is exactly two per iteration after the first (per-participant, for two participants), that the theta seeding the first adaptation on each side is the theta that was passed, that no theta the driver used ever left the interval, that the low bound was actually REACHED so the clamp is a path the default takes on an ordinary problem rather than dead code, and that not every adaptation sat on a bound. Only the LOW bound is reached at this setting; the high bound's end-to-end count is printed for the record and not asserted. The run is observed by wrapping _aitken in a recorder that returns the real function's values verbatim, and the wrapping is PROVEN inert rather than asserted to be: the same case runs first with the driver untouched and the recorded run must match its convergence flag, iteration count and interface temperature exactly.

_mutation.note: Lower the floor the fixture asserts against to a value the driver does not use. The driver still returns exactly 0.05 for an unclamped -50, so the unit assertion fires, and no adaptation in the real run equals 0.01 either, so clamp_low_exercised_end_to_end prints False as well. A fixture that only checked 'theta stayed inside some interval' would survive this, because 0.05 is inside [0.01, 1.0] — pinning the bound is the whole point.

Widen the ceiling the fixture asserts against, the other half of the same claim. The driver returns exactly 1.0 for an unclamped +50 and +1000, so clamp_high_respected prints False. Note that the containment check every_theta_within_the_bounds still passes under this mutation — being inside [0.05, 2.0] is a weaker statement than being clamped at 1.0 — which is exactly why the fixture pins the bound rather than only bracketing it.
